items.stimulus: <u>At the outset,</u> planners assumed that restoring the Chicago River would require rebuilding its banks throughout the city. However, surveys showed that many native plants had survived in protected stretches along the river. Consequently, crews prioritized removing invasive species rather than reconstructing every bank. In addition, the project created walking paths that allowed residents to observe the recovering habitat. At last, after several years of work, fish and bird populations began to increase.

items.stem:
<u>Because</u> Anning lacked formal scientific training and women were often excluded from scientific societies, she had few opportunities to present her findings herself. <u>Nevertheless,</u> geologists relied on the fossils she collected and prepared. Her discoveries helped establish a clearer understanding of prehistoric marine reptiles. <u>As a result,</u> later accounts of paleontology increasingly recognized Anning's contributions. Museums now display many specimens connected to her work.

items.stem:
Her first detailed map of the North Atlantic, published in 1957, showed a long valley running along the ocean's center. As a result, the map challenged the prevailing idea that the ocean floor was mostly flat and featureless. Later, Tharp extended her mapping work to other oceans and produced increasingly detailed images of the global seafloor. Nevertheless, some scientists initially dismissed her interpretation of the central valley as an imaginative mistake. Eventually, evidence from sonar surveys and the theory of plate tectonics confirmed that Tharp's maps had accurately represented a major geological feature.

Which choice provides the most effective transition?
items.stimulus: Marie Tharp was an American geologist and cartographer whose maps helped reveal the structure of the ocean floor. <u>At first,</u> she worked as a geologist on land while studying the Atlantic Ocean through data collected by other researchers. However, women were often excluded from research vessels, so Tharp could not personally visit the locations she was mapping. Because of this, Tharp analyzed thousands of depth measurements gathered by male colleagues. In addition, she compared those measurements with the locations of earthquakes to identify patterns beneath the ocean.
items.explanation: The sentence describes the initial stage of Tharp's career, so "At first," establishes the necessary chronological relationship.

per_choice.correct: The sentence describes the initial stage of Tharp's career, so "At first," establishes the necessary chronological relationship.
per_choice.trap: "As a result," may seem attractive because Tharp's early work led to later discoveries, but the sentence emphasizes when this work occurred rather than its consequence.
